response.text:
Before starting the blade, operators need to lower the guard so it sits within the recommended distance from the workpiece. Even so, the tensioning wheel should be checked at regular points during the shift no matter how the guard is set, since tension can shift over time even if the machine hasn't been running continuously.

Any time the blade is replaced, the lower blade guide should be checked for wear. The exception is when the new blade matches the old one in width and pitch — in that case, a visual inspection is enough, as long as the operator has already gone through the tensioning steps covered elsewhere in this manual.

Operators shouldn't wear loose clothing or jewelry around the machine, and long hair needs to be tied back. Workers can only step away from the work area once the blade has fully stopped, and even then they should be careful, since the machine can stay hot for several minutes afterward.
